units.translation: 123-29a. As when in the folds: just as wolves attacking an unguarded flock are at a loss which to seize first, so the chiefs routed the Bebrycians. Similar to this is the simile in Homer (Il. 16.352-3): 'as wolves, ravenous, fell upon lambs or kids.' He says 'countless' meaning many. 'Grey' means either dark-grey or honored; for the animal is honored among the Athenians: the man who kills a wolf collects for it the means for its burial. And perhaps, since Leto, being pregnant, came to Delos in twelve days after changing into a wolf, therefore at a certain fixed time of the year every she-wolf gives birth in twelve days, as Philostephanus says in his Commentaries (fr. 32 M. III 33).

b. Secretly, of good hides: he says this because on account of the cold both shepherds and dogs sink into the folds; then thus unguarded they harm the sheep. 'Of good hides' means either of good skins—for 'rhinos' is the skin—or <...> properly because they track wild beasts with their noses; therefore hunters take care to lead out the dogs to the hunt before daybreak, so that before the sun rises they may easily track with their noses.
c. <Of good hides:> of keen senses, of keen smell. Lg
d. They seek: they search for. Lg P

e. Often glancing about: often looking around and with excitement; for 'pamphalan' means to look around with agitation. The word is used also by Hipponax (fr. 131 B. II 498) and Anacreon (fr. 160 B. III 293). Erycius also says: 'glancing everywhere they whirled with their feet.' One must reject Irenaeus (fr. 19 Haupt Opusc. II 439) who writes 'amphaphoōntes' and interprets it as 'killing.' For no one uses the word thus, nor is the poet's reading simply that.
f. Around themselves: he should have said 'falling around one another'; for not around themselves. The error is of those after Homer. Lg P

130-31a. As a swarm of bees: because bees flee smoke on account of their narrow sense of smell; which also happens to snakes when deer horn is burned, as Nicander says (Ther. 35 sq.). A swarm is the multitude of bees.
15b. Like bees, he says, they fled, which when smoked fly away. Lg (P)
132-34a. 'With buzzing' instead of with sound and buzzing. A buzz is the sound of bees, but some say of the †boxynou† so-called bee.
b. Smoky: sooty. The sense: furthermore, being smoked by the smoky and ashy smoke they withdraw from the hives. A hive is the vessel into which the honeycombs are gathered, the beehive.
